parsed.title: Discussion on AI in Job Search and Development

claims.text: The author plans to set up automation (OpenClaw) for finding vacancies, generating PDFs of resumes, and writing cover letters.
Having AI‑related skills (Cursor, Claude Code, LLM, RAG, embeddings) is now essential for job seekers in 2026.
The acceleration of development with AI started in 2025, with tools becoming both better and more expensive.
AI‑generated code can introduce serious performance and security issues, as illustrated by a 450‑line raw SQL query that caused 10‑20 min production queries.
Some participants view AI as a market mainstream and believe lack of AI knowledge makes job search harder for JS/Python developers.
Developers sometimes rely on GPT to generate joins and other code, which can speed up routine work.
In one case, AI‑generated code (SELECT *) was pushed to production without review, leading to inefficient queries.
Some team members are skeptical that such low‑quality AI code could exist.
The author jokes that the recruiter profession will become extinct and HR should become personnel management.
Search for candidates using keyword matching is considered increasingly detached from reality.
Debugging logs in JUnit could have helped identify repeated issues earlier.
Long‑term context accumulation in a developer's mind cannot be fully captured by simple AI models.
Quality of AI responses is often proportional to the quality of the question and available knowledge.
Several messages are jokes or hypothetical statements and are not treated as facts.
